questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Which of the above statements are correct?
statements: 1. The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is appointed by the Central Government.
2. Certain provisions in the Constitution of India give the Central Government the right to issue directions to the RBI in public interest.
3. The Governor of the RBI draws his power from the RBI Act.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: The Governor of the RBI is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (Central Government) under the RBI Act, 1934, and draws statutory powers from Section 7(2) and other provisions of the RBI Act. Statement 2 is incorrect because the power to issue directions to the RBI in public interest is granted by Section 7 of the RBI Act, 1934, not by the Constitution of India.

questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Economy question on Banking, RBI & Monetary Policy (Indian Economy / Central Banking).

questions.question:
With reference to casual workers employed in India, consider the following statements:
Which of the above statements are correct?
statements: 1. All casual workers are entitled for Employees Provident Fund coverage.
2. All casual workers are entitled for regular working hours and overtime payment.
3. The government can by a notification specify that an establishment or industry shall pay wages only through its bank account.
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct: Under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, casual and temporary workers are entitled to EPF benefits if they work in a covered establishment (as reaffirmed by the Supreme Court) (1). Under the Minimum Wages Act and labour rules, casual workers are entitled to fixed working hours and overtime wages (2). Under the Payment of Wages (Amendment) Act, 2017, the appropriate government may specify by notification that employers must pay wages solely via bank accounts or cheque (3).
questions.subject: Economy
questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Economy question on Employment, Labour & Poverty (Labour Laws / Social Security).

questions.question: Which among the following steps is most likely to be taken at the time of an economic recession?

options.text: Cut in tax rates accompanied by increase in interest rate
Increase in expenditure on public projects
Increase in tax rates accompanied by reduction of interest rate
Reduction of expenditure on public projects

questions.explanation: During an economic recession, governments implement counter-cyclical expansionary fiscal policy by increasing expenditure on public works/infrastructure projects (Keynesian stimulus) to inject liquidity, generate employment, and revive aggregate demand.

questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Economy question on Fiscal Policy, Union Budget & Public Debt (Macroeconomics / Fiscal Policy).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Other things remaining unchanged, market demand for a good might increase if
Which of the above statements are correct?
statements: 1. price of its substitute increases
2. price of its complement increases
3. the good is an inferior good and income of the consumers increases
4. its price falls
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: If the price of a substitute good rises, consumers switch to the given good, increasing its demand (1). By the law of demand, if its own price falls, quantity demanded increases (4). Statement 2 is incorrect because an increase in the price of a complement reduces demand. Statement 3 is incorrect because for an inferior good, an increase in consumer income decreases demand.

questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Economy question on National Income, GDP & Economic Growth (Microeconomics / Market Demand).

questions.question:
With reference to 'Urban Cooperative Banks' in India, consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 1. They are supervised and regulated by local boards set up by the State Governments.
2. They can issue equity shares and preference shares.
3. They were brought under the purview of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 through an Amendment in 1966.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: UCBs are regulated and supervised by the Reserve Bank of India (for banking functions) and the Registrar of Cooperative Societies/Central Registrar (for incorporation and management), not by local boards set up by State Governments. Statement 2 is correct: Under the Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2020, cooperative banks may issue equity shares, preference shares, and special shares. Statement 3 is correct: Cooperative banks were brought under the regulatory purview of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 with effect from 1 March 1966 via an amendment inserting Section 56.

questions.question:
Indian Government Bond Yields are influenced by which of the following?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. Actions of the United States Federal Reserve
2. Actions of the Reserve Bank of India
3. Inflation and short-term interest rates
questions.explanation: All three factors influence Indian G-sec bond yields: US Federal Reserve rate hikes affect capital flows and currency pressure (1); RBI monetary policy (repo rate and OMOs) directly determines domestic liquidity and yields (2); and inflation expectations and domestic short-term interest rates dictate required nominal bond yields (3).

questions.question:
Consider the following:
Which of the above can be included in Foreign Direct Investments?
statements: 1. Foreign currency convertible bonds
2. Foreign institutional investment with certain conditions
3. Global depository receipts
4. Non-resident external deposits
questions.explanation: According to the Mayaram Committee recommendations on rationalizing foreign investment definitions: Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds (FCCBs) upon conversion, Global Depository Receipts (GDRs/ADRs), and Foreign Portfolio/Institutional Investments where a foreign investor holds 10% or more of the post-issue paid-up equity capital are categorized under Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). Non-Resident External (NRE) deposits are external debt/banking capital liabilities, not FDI.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
The effect of devaluation of a currency is that it necessarily
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
statements: 1. improves the competitiveness of the domestic exports in the foreign markets
2. increases the foreign value of domestic currency
3. improves the trade balance
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Devaluation lowers the price of domestic goods in foreign currency terms, directly enhancing export price competitiveness. Statement 2 is incorrect because devaluation decreases (not increases) the external value of domestic currency. Statement 3 is incorrect because trade balance improvement depends on the price elasticity of exports and imports (Marshall-Lerner condition); it does not 'necessarily' improve trade balance.

questions.question: Which one of the following effects of creation of black money in India has been the main cause of worry to the Government of India?

options.text: Diversion of resources to the purchase of real estate and investment in luxury housing
Investment in unproductive activities and purchase of precious stones, jewellery, gold, etc.
Large donations to political parties and growth of regionalism
Loss of revenue to the State Exchequer due to tax evasion

questions.explanation: The primary systemic concern of the government regarding black money generation is large-scale tax evasion, which severely deprives the state exchequer of fiscal revenues needed for public welfare, healthcare, and infrastructure development.

questions.question: Which one of the following is likely to be the most inflationary in its effects?

options.text: Borrowing from the public to finance a budget deficit
Borrowing from the banks to finance a budget deficit
Creation of new money to finance a budget deficit

questions.explanation: Deficit financing through the creation of fresh high-powered reserve money (monetization of deficit / printing currency) expands the monetary base directly without any corresponding increase in output, making it the most potent cause of inflation.

questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Economy question on Inflation & Price Indices (Macroeconomics / Inflation).

questions.question: The money multiplier in an economy increases with which one of the following?

options.text: Increase in the Cash Reserve Ratio in the banks
Increase in the Statutory Liquidity Ratio in the banks
Increase in the banking habit of the people
Increase in the population of the country

questions.explanation: The money multiplier is given by (1 + c) / (c + r). An increase in the banking habit reduces the currency-to-deposit ratio (c), as individuals hold less physical currency and deposit more money into banks, expanding credit creation and increasing the money multiplier.

questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Economy question on Banking, RBI & Monetary Policy (Macroeconomics / Money Multiplier).

questions.question:
With reference to Indian economy, demand-pull inflation can be caused/increased by which of the following?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. Expansionary policies
2. Fiscal stimulus
3. Inflation-indexing wages
4. Higher purchasing power
5. Rising interest rates
questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand outpaces aggregate supply. Expansionary monetary policy (1), fiscal stimulus (2), and higher consumer purchasing power (4) all boost aggregate demand. Inflation-indexed wages typically cause cost-push inflation (wage-price spiral, 3). Rising interest rates depress borrowing and curb aggregate demand (5).
questions.subject: Economy
questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Economy question on Inflation & Price Indices (Macroeconomics / Inflation Types).

questions.question:
With reference to India, consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 1. Retail investors through demat account can invest in 'Treasury Bills' and 'Government of India Debt Bonds' in primary market.
2. The 'Negotiated Dealing System-Order Matching' is a government securities trading platform of the Reserve Bank of India.
3. The 'Central Depository Services Ltd.' is jointly promoted by the Reserve Bank of India and the Bombay Stock Exchange.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Retail investors can directly participate in the primary auction of T-Bills and G-Secs via the RBI Retail Direct scheme and stock exchange demat mechanisms (1), and NDS-OM is an electronic order-matching trading system for government securities owned by the RBI (2). Statement 3 is incorrect: CDSL was promoted by the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) jointly with leading commercial banks (SBI, Bank of India, etc.), not by the RBI.

questions.question:
With reference to 'WaterCredit', consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above are correct?
statements: 1. It puts microfinance tools to work in the water and sanitation sector.
2. It is a global initiative launched under the aegis of the World Health Organization and the World Bank.
3. It aims to enable the poor people to meet their water needs without depending on subsidies.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: WaterCredit is an initiative pioneered by Water.org (co-founded by Gary White and Matt Damon) that uses microfinance to provide affordable, small loans for clean water connections and household sanitation without depending on traditional subsidies. Statement 2 is incorrect: It was established by the non-profit organization Water.org, not by the WHO and the World Bank.

questions.question:
In India, the central bank's function as the 'lender of last resort' usually refers to which of the following?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. Lending to trade and industry bodies when they fail to borrow from other sources
2. Providing liquidity to the banks having a temporary crisis
3. Lending to governments to finance budgetary deficits
questions.explanation: The 'lender of last resort' function strictly denotes the central bank stepping in to provide emergency liquidity assistance to solvent commercial banks experiencing temporary liquidity shortages or runs, preventing systemic banking collapse. It does not refer to commercial lending to businesses or fiscal deficit financing.

ecological management of 'Wetlands of International Importance' under the Ramsar Convention
sustainable practices in the cultivation of agricultural crops in degraded lands

questions.question:
Why is there a concern about copper smelting plants?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. They may release lethal quantities of carbon monoxide into environment.
2. The copper slag can cause the leaching of some heavy metals into environment.
3. They may release sulphur dioxide as a pollutant.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Copper ores are predominantly sulfide minerals (e.g. chalcopyrite CuFeS2); roasting and smelting generate enormous emissions of toxic sulphur dioxide (SO2) gas (3). Copper slag contains trace amounts of hazardous heavy metals (arsenic, cadmium, lead) that can leach into soil and groundwater (2). Statement 1 is incorrect: Copper smelting does not emit lethal quantities of carbon monoxide.

questions.question:
With reference to furnace oil, consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above are correct?
statements: 1. It is a product of oil refineries.
2. Some industries use it to generate power.
3. Its use causes sulphur emissions into environment.
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct: Furnace oil (fuel oil) is a heavy residual petroleum fraction obtained from crude oil refining (1). It is used as a fuel in thermal boilers, captive power plants, and marine engines (2). Due to high residual sulfur content (often 2–4%), burning it produces substantial sulfur dioxide (SO2) and particulate emissions (3).

Carbon sequestered in forest biomass and agricultural soils
Carbon contained in petroleum and natural gas

questions.explanation: 'Blue carbon' refers to the carbon captured and stored biologically by the world's coastal and marine ecosystems, predominantly mangroves, tidal marshes, and seagrass meadows.

questions.question:
In the nature, which of the following is/are most likely to be found surviving on a surface without soil?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. Fern
2. Lichen
3. Moss
4. Mushroom
questions.explanation: In primary ecological succession (lithosere), Lichens (symbionts of fungi and algae) and Mosses (bryophytes) act as pioneer species capable of colonizing bare, soil-less rock surfaces. Ferns generally require soil or organic substrates, and mushrooms are saprophytic fungi that need decomposing organic matter.

questions.question:
Consider the following kinds of organisms:
Which of the above are primary producers in the food chains of oceans?
statements: 1. Copepods
2. Cyanobacteria
3. Diatoms
4. Foraminifera
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria (photosynthetic blue-green bacteria) and Diatoms (photosynthetic microalgae/phytoplankton) are autotrophic primary producers in marine food webs (2 and 3). Copepods (small crustaceans) and Foraminifera (heterotrophic amoeboid protists) are primary consumers / zooplankton (1 and 4).

questions.question:
Consider the following animals:
To reduce the chance of being captured by predators, which of the above organisms rolls up/roll up and protects/protect its/their vulnerable parts?
statements: 1. Hedgehog
2. Marmot
3. Pangolin
questions.explanation: Hedgehogs roll into a tight ball presenting an impenetrable sphere of spiny quills (1), and Pangolins curl into a tight armored sphere shielded by overlapping keratin scales (3) when threatened. Marmots are large ground squirrels that flee into underground burrows and do not curl up into a defensive ball (2).

questions.question:
With reference to the 'New York Declaration on Forests', which of the following statements are correct?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. It was first endorsed at the United Nations Climate Summit in 2014.
2. It endorses a global timeline to end the loss of forests.
3. It is a legally binding international declaration.
4. It is endorsed by governments, big companies and indigenous communities.
5. India was one of the signatories at its inception.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2, and 4 are correct: NYDF was endorsed at the UN Climate Summit in New York in 2014 (1), set a voluntary target to halve deforestation by 2020 and end natural forest loss by 2030 (2), and was signed by governments, multinational corporations, civil society, and indigenous groups (4). Statement 3 is incorrect because it is a non-legally binding political declaration. Statement 5 is incorrect because India did not sign the declaration.

questions.question:
Magnetite particles, suspected to cause neurodegenerative problems, are generated as environmental pollutants from which of the following?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. Brakes of motor vehicles
2. Engines of motor vehicles
3. Microwave stoves within homes
4. Power plants
5. Telephone lines
questions.explanation: Anthropogenic airborne nanoscale magnetite (Fe3O4) particles originate from high-temperature combustion and friction: vehicle brake pads through abrasive wear (1), diesel and petrol engine combustion (2), and coal-fired power plants (4). Microwave ovens and telephone lines do not generate airborne particulate magnetite emissions. (UPSC official key: b).

questions.question: In case of which one of the following biogeochemical cycles, the weathering of rocks is the main source of release of nutrient to enter the cycle?
questions.explanation: Unlike gaseous biogeochemical cycles (carbon and nitrogen) which have atmospheric reservoirs, the phosphorus cycle is a sedimentary cycle whose primary reservoir is phosphate rocks; mechanical and chemical weathering of rocks releases inorganic phosphate into soil and aquatic ecosystems.

questions.question:
Which of the following are detritivores?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. Earthworms
2. Jellyfish
3. Millipedes
4. Seahorses
5. Woodlice
questions.explanation: Detritivores are heterotrophs that consume decomposing plant and animal parts (detritus) and faeces: Earthworms (1), Millipedes (3), and Woodlice (terrestrial isopods) (5) are classic detritivores. Jellyfish and seahorses are carnivorous predators that feed on live plankton, small fish, and crustaceans.

enabling commercial farming entities around the world to enter carbon emission trading
enabling governments to assess the overall carbon footprint caused by their countries
assessing the overall carbon footprint caused by the use of fossil fuels by the world in a unit time

questions.question:
Which of the following have species that can establish symbiotic relationship with other organisms?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. Cnidarians
2. Fungi
3. Protozoa
questions.explanation: All three have well-documented symbiotic species: 1. Cnidarians form mutualistic symbioses with photosynthetic zooxanthellae dinoflagellates (coral reef mutualism) and with clownfish (sea anemones). 2. Fungi form lichens (with algae/cyanobacteria) and mycorrhizae (with plant roots). 3. Protozoa form mutualisms (e.g. hypermastigote flagellates in termite guts aiding cellulose digestion).

questions.question:
With reference to Chausath Yogini Temple situated near Morena, consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above are correct?
statements: 1. It is a circular temple built during the reign of Kachchhapaghata Dynasty.
2. It is the only circular temple built in India.
3. It was meant to promote the Vaishnava cult in the region.
4. Its design has given rise to a popular belief that it was the inspiration behind the Indian Parliament building.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: The Chausath Yogini temple at Mitawali (Morena district, MP) is a hypaethral circular stone temple built in 1323 CE by King Devapala of the Kachchhapaghata dynasty (1), and its circular pillared design is popularly believed to have inspired Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker's design for Parliament House (Samvidhan Sadan) (4). Statement 2 is incorrect because other circular temples exist in India (e.g. Chausath Yogini temple at Ranipur Jharial and Hirapur in Odisha). Statement 3 is incorrect because it is dedicated to Shiva and 64 Tantric Yoginis (Shaivite/Shakta cult), not Vaishnavism.

questions.question: Which one of the following ancient towns is well-known for its elaborate system of water harvesting and management by building a series of dams and channelizing water into connected reservoirs?

questions.question:
In the first quarter of seventeenth century, in which of the following was/were the factory/factories of the English East India Company located?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
statements: 1. Broach
2. Chicacole
3. Trichinopoly
questions.explanation: In the first quarter of the 17th century (up to 1625), following Thomas Roe's embassy, the English East India Company established subordinate trading factories at Surat (1612), Agra, Ahmedabad, and Broach (Bharuch) in western India, and Masulipatnam (1611) on the Coromandel coast. Chicacole (Srikakulam) and Trichinopoly (Tiruchirappalli) were established much later.

From the decline of Guptas until the rise of Harshavardhana in the early seventh century, which of the following kingdoms were holding power in Northern India?

3. The Pushyabhutis of Thanesar
4. The Maukharis of Kanauj
5. The Yadavas of Devagiri
6. The Maitrakas of Valabhi
questions.explanation: During the 6th and early 7th centuries (interregnum between Imperial Guptas and Harsha): The Later Guptas of Magadha (1), the Pushyabhutis of Thanesar (3), the Maukharis of Kanauj (4), and the Maitrakas of Valabhi in Saurashtra (6) ruled northern and western India. questions.question:

statements: 1. It was during the reign of Iltutmish that Chengiz Khan reached the Indus in pursuit of the fugitive Khwarezm prince.
2. It was during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq that Taimur occupied Multan and crossed the Indus.
3. It was during the reign of Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara Empire that Vasco da Gama reached the coast of Kerala.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above are correct?
statements: 1. St. Francis Xavier was one of the founding members of the Jesuit Order.
2. St. Francis Xavier died in Goa and a church is dedicated to him there.

questions.question: With reference to the history of ancient India, which of the following statements is/are correct?
statements: 1. Mitakshara was the civil law for upper castes and Dayabhaga was the civil law for lower castes.

3. The Mitakshara system deals with the matters related to the property held by male members only of a family, whereas the Dayabhaga system deals with the matters related to the property held by both male and female members of a family.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct: Under the Mitakshara school (Vijnaneshwara), a son acquires a birthright in ancestral coparcenary property during the father's lifetime; under the Dayabhaga school (Jimutavahana), a son acquires rights in family property only upon the death of the father. Statements 1 and 3 are incorrect: The division between Mitakshara and Dayabhaga is territorial (Dayabhaga in Bengal/Assam; Mitakshara in the rest of India), not caste-based, and both deal with succession and women's property rights (stridhana).

questions.question:
How is permaculture farming different from conventional chemical farming?

questions.explanation: Global freshwater distribution: Glaciers and polar ice caps contain ~68.7% of all freshwater (~1.7% of total global water). Groundwater accounts for ~30.1% of freshwater (~0.76% of total global water). Surface freshwater in rivers and freshwater lakes constitutes only ~0.009% of total global water. Hence, water in ice caps and glaciers is far greater than groundwater (Statement 2 is correct), while water in rivers and lakes is far less than groundwater (Statement 1 is incorrect).

In a pressure cooker, the temperature at which the food is cooked depends mainly upon which of the following?

Statement 2 is correct: Based on the recommendations of the First Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC, 1966), a separate Department of Personnel was created in the Cabinet Secretariat in 1970 directly under the Prime Minister.

questions.question: 'Right to Privacy' is protected under which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017), a nine-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court unanimously affirmed that the Right to Privacy is an intrinsic fundamental right guaranteed under Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty) as well as the overarching freedoms in Part III.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 1. In India, there is no law restricting the candidates from contesting in one Lok Sabha election from three constituencies.
2. In 1991 Lok Sabha Election, Shri Devi Lal contested from three Lok Sabha constituencies.

3. As per the existing rules, if a candidate contests in one Lok Sabha election from many constituencies, his/her party should bear the cost of bye-elections to the constituencies vacated by him/her in the event of him/her winning in all the constituencies.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: Section 33(7) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (amended in 1996) expressly restricts a candidate from contesting from more than TWO constituencies in any general election or by-election. Statement 2 is correct: In the 1991 general elections (prior to the 1996 amendment), former Deputy Prime Minister Devi Lal contested from three Lok Sabha seats (Rohtak, Ferozepur, and Sikar). Statement 3 is incorrect: There is no existing law or rule requiring a candidate's political party to bear the expenses of bye-elections for vacated seats (though the Election Commission has proposed such a reform).
questions.subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Polity question on Parliament, Legislative Procedures, or Committees (Indian Polity / Elections & Representation).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 1. 'Right to the City' is an agreed human right and the UN-Habitat monitors the commitments made by each country in this regard.
2. 'Right to the City' gives every occupant of the city the right to reclaim public spaces and public participation in the city.
3. 'Right to the City' means that the State cannot deny any public service or facility to the unauthorized colonies in the city.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: The 'Right to the City' was recognized within the New Urban Agenda (Habitat III, 2016) monitored by UN-Habitat (1), emphasizing the democratic right of all city inhabitants to access, inhabit, and reclaim public spaces and engage in urban decision-making (2). Statement 3 is incorrect because the Right to the City does not legally prohibit states from denying public facilities to illegal or unauthorized structures. (UPSC official key: c or d; official key finalized c or d).

questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Polity question on Statutory and Regulatory Bodies (Human Rights / Urban Governance).

questions.question:
With reference to India, consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 1. Judicial custody means an accused is in the custody of the concerned magistrate and such accused is locked up in police station, not in jail.
2. During judicial custody, the police officer in charge of the case is not allowed to interrogate the suspect without the approval of the court.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: In police custody, the suspect is held in a police lockup under the physical custody of police officers. In judicial custody, the accused is under the custody of the magistrate and is lodged in central/district jail, not in a police station. Statement 2 is correct: Once an accused is remanded to judicial custody, police investigators cannot interrogate the accused without prior formal permission from the competent magistrate/court.
questions.subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Polity question on Judiciary, Courts, or Legal System (Indian Polity / Criminal Justice System).

questions.question:
With reference to India, consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 1. When a prisoner makes out a sufficient case, parole cannot be denied to such prisoner because it becomes a matter of his/her right.
2. State Governments have their own Prisoners Release on Parole Rules.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Supreme Court has repeatedly affirmed that parole is a privilege/concession and not an absolute fundamental or legal right of a convict. Statement 2 is correct: Under Entry 4 of the State List, 'Prisons' is a State subject, and each State Government frames its own Prisons Rules / Prisoners Release on Parole Rules.

questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Polity question on Judiciary, Courts, or Legal System (Indian Polity / Prison Administration).

questions.question: At the national level, which ministry is the nodal agency to ensure effective implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006?

options.text: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

questions.explanation: Under Section 11 of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and the Allocation of Business Rules, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) is the designated nodal central agency for the implementation of the Act.

questions.question: A legislation which confers on the executive or administrative authority an unguided and uncontrolled discretionary power in the matter of application of law violates which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Under Indian constitutional jurisprudence, unguided, arbitrary, and uncontrolled discretionary power conferred upon the executive violates the Rule of Law and the doctrine of equality and non-arbitrariness enshrined in Article 14 of the Constitution (as established in State of West Bengal v. Anwar Ali Sarkar and E.P. Royappa).

questions.question: Which one of the following in Indian polity is an essential feature that indicates that it is federal in character?

options.text: The independence of judiciary is safeguarded.
The Union Legislature has elected representatives from constituent units.
The Union Cabinet can have elected representatives from regional parties.
The Fundamental Rights are enforceable by Courts of Law.

questions.explanation: In federal polities, an independent judiciary is an indispensable structural feature to umpire and adjudicate disputes between the federal government and constituent units, and to uphold the supremacy of the dual constitutional division of powers.

questions.question: Which one of the following best defines the term 'State'?

options.text: A community of persons permanently occupying a definite territory independent of external control and possessing an organized government
A politically organized people of a definite territory and possessing an authority to govern them, maintain law and order, protect their natural rights and safeguard their means of sustenance
A number of persons who have been living in a definite territory for a very long time with their own culture, tradition and government
A society permanently living in a definite territory with a central authority, an executive responsible to the central authority and an independent judiciary

questions.explanation: In political science (Garner's classic definition), a 'State' consists of four essential, indispensable constituent elements: Population (community of persons), Territory (definite territory), Government (organized government), and Sovereignty (independence of external control).

questions.question:
With reference to Indian judiciary, consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 1. Any retired judge of the Supreme Court of India can be called back to sit and act as a Supreme Court judge by the Chief Justice of India with prior permission of the President of India.
2. A High Court in India has the power to review its own judgement as the Supreme Court does.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: 1. Under Article 128 of the Constitution, the Chief Justice of India may, with the previous consent of the President, request any retired Supreme Court or Federal Court judge to sit and act as a Judge of the Supreme Court. 2. As courts of record under Article 215, High Courts in India possess inherent power to review their own judgments (as reaffirmed in Shivdeo Singh v. State of Punjab), analogous to the review power under Article 137.
questions.subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Polity question on President, Vice-President, or Governor (Indian Polity / Judiciary).

questions.question:
With reference to India, consider the following statements:
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 1. There is only one citizenship and one domicile.
2. A citizen by birth only can become the Head of State.
3. A foreigner once granted the citizenship cannot be deprived of it under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: In Pradeep Jain v. Union of India (1984), the Supreme Court held that the Constitution recognizes only one single citizenship and one single domicile for all of India. Statement 2 is incorrect: Under Article 58, any Indian citizen (whether by birth, descent, registration, or naturalization) is eligible to be elected President (Head of State), unlike the US requirement of being a natural-born citizen. Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Section 10 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, naturalized or registered citizens can be deprived of citizenship on grounds of fraud, disloyalty to the Constitution, or trading with an enemy during war.
questions.subject: Indian Polity and Governance
questions.classification_rationale: GS1 Polity question on Constitutional Provisions, Schedules, Amendments, or Emergency (Indian Polity / Citizenship).

questions.question: Which one of the following factors constitutes the best safeguard of liberty in a liberal democracy?
questions.explanation: As articulated by Montesquieu and classical constitutionalists, the Separation of Powers (and system of checks and balances among the legislature, executive, and judiciary) prevents the concentration of tyrannical power in any single branch, serving as the paramount structural safeguard of individual liberty.

questions.question: Under the Indian Constitution, concentration of wealth violates

options.text: the Directive Principles of State Policy

questions.explanation: Article 39(c) of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) directs the State to ensure that 'the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth and means of production to the common detriment'.

questions.question: What is the position of the Right to Property in India?

options.text: Legal right available to citizens only
Legal right available to any person
Fundamental Right available to citizens only
Neither Fundamental Right nor legal right

questions.explanation: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 repealed the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right (Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31) and re-enacted it as a constitutional/legal right under Article 300A, which states that 'No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law', making it available to 'any person' (citizens and non-citizens/corporations alike).

questions.question: What was the exact constitutional status of India on 26th January, 1950?

options.text: A Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic

questions.explanation: On 26 January 1950, the original Preamble declared India to be a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'. The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' (along with 'and Integrity') were subsequently inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.

questions.question: Constitutional government means

a government whose Head enjoys nominal powers
a government whose Head enjoys real powers
a government limited by the terms of the Constitution

questions.explanation: A constitutional government is defined by constitutionalism: it is a limited government whose powers and authority are defined, circumscribed, and limited by the fundamental law of the land (the Constitution).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements in respect of Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards:
Which of the above statements are not correct?
statements: 1. Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards are titles under the Article 18(1) of the Constitution of India.
2. Padma Awards, which were instituted in the year 1954, were suspended only once.
3. The number of Bharat Ratna Awards is restricted to a maximum of five in a particular year.
questions.explanation: All three statements are incorrect: 1. In Balaji Raghavan v. UOI (1995), the Supreme Court ruled that National Awards do not amount to 'titles' prohibited under Article 18(1). 2. The Padma awards have been suspended twice: first from 1977 to 1980 by the Janata Party government, and again from 1992 to 1997 pending litigation in the courts. 3. The number of annual Bharat Ratna awards is restricted to a maximum of three in a particular year (not five). Since all three are incorrect, the answer is 1, 2 and 3.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
statements: Statement 1: The United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) and the Arbor Day Foundation have recently recognized Hyderabad as 2020 Tree City of the World.
Statement 2: Hyderabad was selected for the recognition for a year following its commitment to grow and maintain the urban forests.

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct and Statement 2 is the correct explanation for Statement 1
Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is correct but Statement 2 is not correct
Statement 1 is not correct but Statement 2 is correct

questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: The 'Tree Cities of the World' programme is organized by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the Arbor Day Foundation, not the UNCDF. questions.question:
Consider the following statements in respect of the Laureus World Sports Award which was instituted in the year 2000:

statements: 1. American golfer Tiger Woods was the first winner of this award.
2. The award was received mostly by 'Formula One' players so far.
3. Roger Federer received this award maximum number of times compared to others.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Tiger Woods won the inaugural Laureus World Sportsman of the Year award in 2000 (1); and Swiss tennis champion Roger Federer has won the Sportsman of the Year award five times (plus one Comeback award, totalling six Laureus statuettes), more than any other individual (3). Statement 2 is incorrect: Tennis players (Federer, Nadal, Djokovic) have won the award most frequently, not Formula One drivers.

statements: 1. The official motto for this Olympics is 'A New World'.
2. Sport Climbing, Surfing, Skateboarding, Karate and Baseball are included in this Olympics.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: The official motto of the 32nd Summer Olympic Games (Tokyo 2020) was 'United by Emotion' ('A New World' was the motto of Rio 2016). questions.question:
Consider the following statements in respect of the ICC World Test Championship:
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
statements: 1. The finalists were decided by the number of matches they won.
2. New Zealand was ranked ahead of England because it won more matches than England.
questions.explanation: Both statements are incorrect: Due to disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, the ICC altered the qualification criteria so that the finalists for the 2019–2021 World Test Championship were ranked on the basis of percentage of points (PCT) won, not total number of matches won (invalidating Statement 1). England actually won 11 matches, while New Zealand won only 7 matches, but New Zealand qualified for the final ahead of England because New Zealand had a higher percentage of points contested (70.0% vs. England's 61.4%) (invalidating Statement 2).
